history.summary: CSV town 'Tinsukia' is the district/nearest city, not the exact locality - the temple stands at Bordubi village, about 50-60 km from Tinsukia town, so the town field is corrected to Bordubi. Per local accounts, in 1965 tea garden workers found a Shiva linga emerging from the soil near a peepal/banyan tree at Bordubi; the garden administration built a small shrine around it. Devotees who found their wishes fulfilled returned with bells, creating the signature tradition: thousands of bronze, brass, copper and aluminium bells (some weighing up to ~55 kg) now hang on iron frameworks installed to protect the tree. The temple has three bell-shaped domes and is reported (verify) to be recorded in the Limca Book of Records for the largest collection of bells. Mondays are especially busy.

name: Tilinga Mandir (Bell Temple)
town_description: Bordubi is a tea-garden village in Tinsukia district, Upper Assam, on the road between Tinsukia town and Margherita. Like much of this region it sits amid tea estates and oil country, with Dibrugarh and Tinsukia as the nearest urban centres.

travel.railway: Tinsukia Railway Station; local road transport to Bordubi
travel.road: On SH-23 at Bordubi, about 50-60 km from Tinsukia town via Naharkatia; well signposted locally

visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM-7:00 PM daily, 6:30 AM on Mondays (verify locally)
